case.summary: Case HHG-005 on card C02923-K1 is closed as legitimate at a probability of 0.04 (pattern: none) after the customer confirmed transaction 3523199, a $100.07 online purchase in product R on 2016-12-07. The episode is the single transaction 3523199, exposure $0.00 (no block, so nothing carried against the customer). Decisive evidence: the history family showed the amount sits well inside the card's baseline (median $117.01, max $1,104.08) in the card's modal home region 330.0, and the calibrated case-memory score (cms_p 0.026) sharply contradicted the raw risk_score of 0.54; the device family confirmed the New iOS profile is a generic, non-strong device (112 cards all-time) with no card-testing, burst, or shared-origin signal. A customer_validation request was asked because this was a single weak signal (risk_score alone) under R1; the assumed reply was a confirmation that the purchase and new phone were the customer's own, satisfying R3 and settling the case (customer family). Similar cleared same-region cases CC-2403, CC-4000 and CC-2091 supported the legitimate reading, while the card's three prior confirmed account_takeover cases (CC-2400, CC-2717, CC-2857) were considered but did not share method or timing with this isolated purchase. The alternative reading — treating the New device and prior account-takeover history as decisive and denying the transaction — would have triggered R2 (BLOCK_CARD, CREATE_CASE) had the customer instead denied it; that did not occur. Recommended route: auto — CREATE_CASE, ALLOW_TRANSACTION, CLOSE_NO_FRAUD, no L1/L2 approval needed.
